::: {.notes}
This is an excerpt of the unnumbered evaluation table in the V9.5 release article. “Genre expressed” is Mureka’s fully expressed genre rate. “Listening pass” is the overall listening pass rate. The final row is the mean audio-quality pass rate. Mureka labels the comparator only as its previous baseline. Changes are differences in percentage points. The publisher does not give rater counts or its exact pass rules. [Mureka · Song evaluation](https://www.mureka.ai/blog_en/mureka-v9-5-model-changes.html#song-evaluation-the-v95-capability-profile).

The release article’s “Song evaluation” table separates overall usability from prompt control and vocal pass rates. These are separately reported criteria across the 100-song evaluation. They are not successive filtering stages. The public article leaves the rater count and exact pass criteria unspecified.

The exact scope is Mureka V9.5, with API ID mureka-9.5. The release date follows the official changelog, 28 August 2026; the vendor press release followed on 31 August (row 6). Mureka is from Kunlun Tech.

The vendor blog names MusiCoT and describes organizing a whole song before developing sections, melody, vocals and arrangement (row 8). That is Partial architecture evidence. The linked MusiCoT paper is method context: its CLAP thoughts, MeLoDy system, roughly one-billion-parameter language model and diffusion component must not be assigned to V9.5 without version-specific evidence. “O3 reflective reasoning” and a “MuCo creation agent” appear only in Pandaily metadata; the official changelog lists o1 and o2, not O3. The workbook marks that row as rumor, and this card does not promote it into a model fact (row 10).

The official API reference could not be extracted in the source audit. Lyrics up to 5,000 characters, style/gender controls, reference_id, vocal_id, melody_id, MP3/WAV/FLAC, and the $0.225 song price come from reseller WaveSpeed, not official Mureka documentation (rows 7, 29–30): https://wavespeed.ai/models/mureka-ai/mureka-v9.5/generate-song. The maximum song length is unreported; a 5:14 demo is not a limit (row 28). Earlier changelog support for ten languages, multiple results and streaming is family-level context; applicability to mureka-9.5 is not separately documented (rows 31–32).

The vendor’s evaluation uses 100 songs against an unnamed baseline: vocal pass 53→61%, prompt control 92→97%, genre 84.9→95.7%, overall listening 34→35%, audio health 81→84%, usability 25→28%. These are developer claims without a published protocol, not an independent benchmark (row 27). More than 25,000 survey responses guided product improvements, but the release does not say those responses were training data (row 17).

Tools are Known at the Mureka platform level: generation, extension, recognition, description, stems, transcription, reference voice/accompaniment, soundtracks and remix/video services (rows 36–40). This does not imply every historical endpoint is a native V9.5 mechanism. Public weights are not found (row 41).

Snapshot provenance: Music_v1.0.xlsx, sheet “Mureka V9.5”, audit 19.10.2026. The five category statuses reproduce the workbook’s summary judgment; they are not a majority vote over detail rows or a quality ranking. This card converts the supplied audit and does not certify the sources afresh. “Not disclosed” means not found in that audit’s accessible materials, not proof that the capability is absent.
